name: Crack a fetch on turn 1-2 for a land that unlocks a hand card
intent: On turn 1 or 2, once open-land-unlocks has had first refusal, play a fetch from hand and crack it for whatever land in the library would unlock some other hand card - Marsh Flats found for a library Swamp that lets Thoughtseize be cast. instant-reanimator carries exactly one copy each of Island, Plains and Swamp, so every fetch (Flooded Strand, Marsh Flats, Polluted Delta) reaches two of the three, equally live - no fetch is more precious than another the way a scarcer basic makes one elsewhere in this pass (dimir-frog, esper-blink, boros-aggro), so which one is played is left to ties: any, by sorted name. Triggers on unlocks_by_basic_search, not the broader unlocks_by_search (review item 3): a fetch that can only reach a non-basic unlock (a shockland the library holds but no basic) never makes this play apply at all - open-fetch-unlocks-shock covers exactly that case instead, paying the shock's own 2 life on top of the fetch's. The crack itself is restricted to an untapped source that can actually reach a basic unlock (searches_for_any plus unlocks_by_basic_search), so a stale fetch already on the battlefield that cannot reach the needed basic is never cracked in place of the one that can. Its own choose_cards pick prefers a shockland with a Plains subtype first - this deck's own dual-colour fixing (Godless Shrine, Hallowed Fountain both carry Plains) outweighs the 2 life this early, ahead of even a free basic (hand Marsh Flats+Polluted Delta+Thoughtseize+Faithful Mending+Goryo's Vengeance+Atraxa with a library Godless Shrine and Swamp both reachable: takes the Shrine) - then a bare basic, then any other shockland, paying life only when the fetch's own find needs it. Stands down once open-land-unlocks would already fire (U's own key), at 7 life or less, and once the library is down to 5 cards or fewer - thinning this early is not worth decking risk later. Only turns 1-2, land drop available, mine, precombat main, empty stack. Stands down once the discard outlet (a creature with an own +1/+1-counter-put ability, Psychic Frog in this 60) is already on the battlefield: that fact is byte-identical to the seat-admitted bin-fatty-vs-permanent-exile play's own battlefield-outlet true key, and it can never hold on a genuine turn 1-2 board anyway - the outlet costs two mana and has to survive a turn cycle before that play reads it as safe to fire, so this key costs this play nothing here and only prevents the two plays overlapping later in the game.
